title: Comprehensive review on thermo‐hydraulic performance enhancement of solar air collector
content:
Abstract

Solar air collector is commonly used for low- and medium-temperature applications like space heating, drying, and various industrial processes, particularly because of their simple design and low operating cost. In this paper, a comprehensive review is made on the novel techniques used to improve the performance of the solar air collector. The performance of the various techniques is examined by numerous heat transfer parameters like Nusselt number enhancement ratio, friction enhancement ratio, thermal efficiency and thermal enhancement ratio. The implementation of artificial roughness in the form of ribs, baffles, fins protrusion, cavities and vortex generators strongly improves the heat transfer and significantly enhances the thermal performance of SAC through strong turbulence and well mixing. For hemispherical cavity rib-turbulators, a maximum Nusselt number enhancement ratio of 5.33 is achieved within the range of parameters considered. Solar air collector with phase change materials strengthens thermal energy storage, outlet temperature stability and operational time with an enhancement in thermal efficiency of 5%–17% in this study. Jet impingement with multi-arc ribs under optimized conditions is concluded as the case that provides a maximum thermal enhancement ratio of 4.1 within the designed parameters. Additionally, it is reported that phase change materials promote the thermal performance of the solar air collector. This study also highlights the impact of geometric and flow parameters that ensure the optimum heat transfer with low frictional losses.
